data.title: DeSantis withdraws death warrant for first time, calling off execution
data.description:
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) is withdrawing a death warrant for the first time since he became governor, calling off the execution of 74-year-old William Lee Thompson following the botched execution of Tennessee inmate Christa Pike. 

DeSantis’s letter to Florida State Prison Warden Randall Polk blocks Thompson’s scheduled execution by lethal injection. In the letter, the Florida governor did not outline any reasoning behind his decision.

Thompson’s attorneys previously raised serious concerns about his mental competency and deteriorating physical health, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Thompson was sentenced to death for his role in the 1976 murder of 23-year-old Sally Ivester.

Thompson was one of two inmates scheduled to be executed on Oct. 13. James Robertson, 63, remains scheduled for execution on Tuesday for the 2008 killing of his cellmate, Frank Hart.

DeSantis’s rare reversal comes after Pike’s failed execution earlier this week where she was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital and survived.

The failed execution of Pike, in which she was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital and survived, has brought renewed scrutiny to the death penalty nationwide, even in states like Florida that have altered their lethal injection procedure to not include pentobarbital.

Pike’s lawyers report that she is alive and speaking but sustained “severe damage” to her arms and remains handcuffed and shackled to a hospital bed and that she was receiving “lifesaving care” in the hospital.

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee (R) has ordered that Pike’s execution be delayed until at least next year.

The U.S. military is also scheduling its first execution in decades of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Thursday the execution would be by firing squad and livestreamed which was criticized by GOP lawmakers – including Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.).

In the past two years, the rate of executions in Florida has increased with 19 in 2025 and 16 in 2026 so far. Previously, the Sunshine State had not executed more than eight inmates in a year, doing so in 1984 and 2014, according to the Florida Department of Corrections. The state currently also leads for the highest number of executions in 2026 so far.

data.title: Southwest Airlines says 'brief' system outage affected boarding, checked bags
data.description:
(NEXSTAR) – Southwest Airlines experienced a “brief” outage on Friday morning that affected the computer systems used to help check baggage and board flights.

Southwest confirmed the news shortly after travelers began to report delays.

“Southwest experienced a brief interruption due to a system outage at our vendor, Amadeus,” a spokesperson for the airline wrote in an emailed statement to Nexstar. “The airline continued to check baggage and board flights manually while full functionality was restored.”

The Amadeus IT Group, referenced in the statement, is a provider of travel software utilized by numerous global airlines.

“Amadeus briefly experienced a technical issue today affecting Southwest Airlines, originating from a third-party technology provider,” the IT company wrote. “Our teams took immediate action and worked closely with the provider to restore normal operations. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.”

Outage-detection platform DownDetector showed that passengers began reporting issues with Southwest shortly before 9 a.m., EDT on Friday.

Travelers claimed on social media that their gate agents were unable to scan their boarding passes, or that workers at the check-in gate were issuing handwritten baggage tickets. Others said they were told that all flights had been halted amid the outage, though the airline has disputed that was the case.

“[Flights were] not halted, just slowed due to manual processes,” a Southwest spokesperson said.

The airline’s initial statement also apologized to affected passengers.

We apologize to our Customers for any inconvenience and working to get them to their destinations as quickly as possible,” a spokesperson wrote. “Nothing is more important to Southwest than the Safety of our Customers and Employees.”

data.title: Trump: Russia will supply US with diesel
data.description:
Russia will supply the U.S. with diesel, President Trump announced on Friday.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.

“Additionally, based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel,” he added. 

The announcement comes as high diesel prices, tied in part to the Iran conflict, have contributed to inflation and have particularly presented issues for farmers. The matter has become a major midterm issue.

Developing.

data.title: Who is Katie Zacharia, potential new White House press secretary?
data.description:
Katie Zacharia, a conservative lawyer and commentator, may be the next person to lead the White House briefing room, having been offered the press secretary position by President Trump.

Zacharia brings a stint as spokesperson and deputy assistant secretary at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Former DHS spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin, in a post on social platform X in February as she resigned, called Zacharia “a dynamic and effective voice in media.”

Zacharia was a commentator for Newsmax and also appeared as a guest on Fox News.

Upon her DHS appointment, Zacharia said she was “honored and proud to serve” President Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem “as the new Spokesperson and Deputy Assistant Secretary for Public Affairs.”

“I will continue to work tirelessly to Make America Great Again!” she added.

Zacharia got her undergraduate and law degrees from Pepperdine University, according to her LinkedIn. While an undergraduate, she interned for the Republican National Committee and in the White House Office of Political Affairs during former President George W. Bush’s second term. 

During law school, she worked at the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas and served as a law clerk to the director of Advocates International, a global network of Christian lawyers that serves the “poor, vulnerable and oppressed,” according to its website.

She also spent time after graduating from law school working internationally at a firm in Beijing and for an organization focused on caring for children of migrant workers. More recently she served on the Dean’s Council Board at Pepperdine Law and as director of development at the school.

Zacharia has also worked as a legal advisor to Fix California, a group looking to advance conservative policies in the Golden State that was founded by Richard Grenell, an ally of President Trump who is currently the interim president of the Kennedy Center.

In a New York Post op-ed published in mid-February, Zacharia called Trump “the greatest president in U.S. history” and criticized liberal activists for “obstructing” the work of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

At the time, ICE and Customs and Border Protection faced scrutiny in the wake of the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal immigration officers in January in Minneapolis, which sparked protests and blowback for the administration.

Originally published on Feb. 18

data.title: Vance on Hegseth plan for live-streamed execution: 'I'm not goig to be watching it'
data.description:
Vice President Vance said on Friday that he will not be watching the execution of Nidal Hasan if the Pentagon follows through on livestreaming the event in December. 

“I’ve seen those announcements. I don’t know if that’s actually going to happen,” Vance told reporters in Lima, Ohio on Friday. 

“This is a guy who committed, in my view, the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9-11,” he continued. “The people that he was meant to treat, the army soldiers he was meant to treat for mental illness and other problems, he took them at their most vulnerable, and gunned down these people where they lived.” 

“So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don’t forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people,” he said. “Now that said, if it’s ultimately livestreamed, I’m not going to be watching it.” 

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Thursday that the public would be able to watch Hasan’s execution by firing squad. 

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” Hegseth said in an interview with the conservative outlet Real America’s Voice. 

The announcement sparked immediate bipartisan backlash. 

“I absolutely support the sentence of death, but live-streaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that,” Rep. Austin Scott (R-Ga.) said in a post on X. 

Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) called the move “disgusting” during an interview on CNN.

“What is he, mimicking ISIS executions?” Murphy said.

data.title: Katie Zacharia offered White House press secretary post
data.description:
President Trump has offered Katie Zacharia, a conservative commentator and communications adviser to the president’s media company, the position as the next White House press secretary, a White House official confirmed to The Hill.

The New York Times first reported on Friday that Zacharia would be named to the post.

Zacharia would fill a role vacated by Trump ally Karoline Leavitt, who left the administration earlier this year after the birth of her second child and subsequently took a job as a commentator on the Fox News Channel.

Zacharia is a former spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security and most recently served as a top communication adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, the company behind the president’s Truth Social platform.

Developing…

data.title: Cities ask Supreme Court to block Texas-DOJ deal invalidating immigration rule
data.description:
Three Democratic-controlled cities on Friday said they asked the Supreme Court to revive an immigration regulation blocked under a deal struck by Texas and the Trump administration, accusing them of “egregious collusion.” 

Texas sued over the Biden-era regulation in June. On the same day, the administration conceded it was unlawful, and a judge quickly entered an order halting implementation nationwide. 

The cities — Baltimore; Columbus, Ohio; and New Haven, Conn. — alongside a legal aid group have been looking to intervene in the litigation to defend the regulation, but lower courts turned them away. It leaves them seeking emergency relief from the justices.

“This case involves an egregious new extension of this phenomenon,” the cities wrote in their application. “The government did not merely leverage a convenient loss to undo agency action, but rather, announced in advance that it would not defend a disfavored regulation and then colluded with the challenger from the moment that suit was filed.” 

The underlying case concerns administrative closure, which gives immigration judges authority to remove certain low-profile cases from their calendars to promote docket efficiency or for other reasons. The cities emphasize that, for example, it allows neglected juveniles to pause their cases as they seek relief.

The practice had existed in some form for years, but Texas’s suit said the Biden-era regulation “drastically expands” it to effectively give people indefinite permission to remain in the country. 

It’s a position supported by the Trump administration, which abandoned defending the regulation.

“But allowing immigration judges to exercise discretion by pausing a case indefinitely— often for decades, if not forever—would subvert Congress’s directive,” the Justice Department wrote to a lower court in the case. 

The cities and the legal aid group — Centro Legal de la Raza — are represented by Democracy Forward Foundation. The group has filed dozens of lawsuits against the Trump administration, becoming one of the most prolific litigators challenging the president’s agenda in court. 

It says Texas and the Justice Department weren’t adverse parties and the lower courts shouldn’t have entertained their deal. 

“The adversity requirement is not a formality,” they wrote in their Supreme Court emergency appeal. 

The cities’ request goes to Justice Samuel Alito, who handles emergency matters arising from Texas by default. He could act alone or refer it to the full court for a vote.

data.title: Vance on Guilfoyle texts: If 'something bad' happened, 'people have to suffer consequences'
data.description:
Vice President Vance weighed in Friday on reporting that U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked one of President Trump’s donors for debt relief in exchange for political access, saying “people have to suffer the consequences” if “something bad happened.”

“Look, these are allegations, and what I always say is: we don’t try people in the court of public opinion. We try people in a court of law,” Vance told reporters during a trip to his home state of Ohio. 

The Wall Street Journal first reported on Wednesday that Guilfoyle allegedly asked Eric Deters to wire $100,000 to American Express without a paper trail ahead and, in exchange, promised to help him reach senior administration officials. The request came just ahead of her confirmation hearing for the Greece ambassadorship before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. 

Deters shot her down, saying it would cost him his marriage, according to messages shared with the Journal, and later obtained by The Hill’s sister network NewsNation.

“You don’t take messages that people allegedly had between one person or another, or one person’s story, and say, ‘Oh, because of that, Kimberly Guilfoyle is, is guilty.’ I think that’s absurd,” Vance said Friday. “Let’s actually see what the facts are. Let’s see what the truth is.”

He added, “And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it.”

The scandal has added scrutiny to advisers in Trump’s orbit. Asked whether the Guilfoyle allegations are “how the administration works,” the vice president said, “certainly not.” 

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, on a diplomatic trip to Greece, also shrugged off reporters’ questions about whether he maintained confidence in Guilfoyle and whether her conduct raised any concerns. 

“Like, our job is not to respond every time someone decides to give the media something without any advance warning, without having any chance to look at it and see what’s in there,” Rubio said.

Vance was in Ohio on Friday to cast his midterm vote and take part in a rally to support Republicans, including incumbent Sen. Jon Husted and GOP gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy, in the Buckeye State.

data.title: Ossoff: Hegseth 'deeply unwell'
data.description:
Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) on Friday called Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth “a deeply unwell person” over his plan to livestream a firing squad execution next month.  

“I think Pete Hegseth is, frankly … a deeply unwell person who seems to relish this kind of brutality,” Ossoff said on MS NOW. 

The Pentagon a day prior revealed a surprise plan to livestream the Dec. 3 firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood, Texas, shooter former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan in what would be the military’s first execution in six decades. The plan immediately drew fierce blowback from both sides of the aisle, who have called the idea barbaric and below the country’s dignity and standards.

“Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting,” Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), wrote on X. “Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America.” 

Joe Kent, the former head of the National Counterterrorism Center who resigned in March over the Iran war, said streaming Hasan’s execution is “a stain on our morality” and “also gives the terrorists free propaganda that they will use to radicalize & recruit more terrorists like Hassan.”

And Senate Armed Services Committee ranking member Jack Reed (D-R.I.), said in a statement that Hegseth’s plan is “a gift to anti-American terrorist recruiters,” and “absolutely shameful and damaging to America’s interests and core values.”

Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, opened fire at Fort Hood in 2009, killing 13 people. He is set to be put to death on Dec. 3 at 1 p.m. local time at the same military base, according to Hegseth.

The last American service member to be put to death by firing squad was Pvt. Edward Donald Slovik, convicted of deserting his unit twice in combat in France. He was executed in the country on Jan. 31, 1945. 

“I kind of like the mentality we had in WWII,  which was win, understand that when the enemy attacks you, you stand your ground,” Hegseth said Thursday.

Since then, the U.S. military has carried out only one other execution with the 1961 hanging of Pvt. John Bennett for rape and attempted murder. The U.S. military has never in modern history made an execution public and the last public execution of anyone in the U.S. was nearly a century ago in 1936.

Osoff accused Hegseth of “spending his time with this kind of obscene medieval spectacle” rather than focusing on running the Pentagon, which he said is “falling into chaos.”

“The folks who are in positions of power in this administration, and of course we know all these things, but their values are in disarray, they’re totally disconnected from the daily experience of the American people, and their foreign policy is endangering the United States, squandering our international power and destroying our image in the world,” he said.

data.title: Ocasio-Cortez set to rally for El-Sayed in Michigan
data.description:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) is scheduled to travel to Michigan next week to campaign alongside Democratic Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed. 

Ocasio-Cortez will make stops in three small towns on the candidate’s “It Shouldn’t Be This Hard” bus tour next Thursday, according to a schedule of events shared by El-Sayed’s campaign. The tour will hit Escanaba, Iron Mountain and Marquette. 

“Abdul has built a winning coalition with an agenda to bring down costs for Michigan families and I could not be more excited to join him for the final stretch of this race,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “Once he’s in Washington, I look forward to working with Abdul to guarantee healthcare as a human right for all Americans and to build a politics that is free from the corrupting influence of corporate money.”

On Friday, the New York Democrat will host her own separate political events at universities in Rochester and Ypsilanti, and a “Latinos for Abdul Rally” in Detroit. 

Ocasio-Cortez has previously campaigned alongside El-Sayed in Michigan and recently appeared at a Democratic fundraiser for his Senate race in New York City. 

El-Sayed called the lawmaker a “critical partner” in his successful primary race. 

“I look forward to campaigning with her over the course of the next 25 days to ensure that Michiganders have a Senator who is committed to putting money in their pocket, getting money out of politics, and passing medicare for all,” he said in a statement.

Several other prominent Democrats have already visited the Wolverine State to stump for the candidate as he seeks to defeat Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Rogers (Mich.), in the November race. 

Last month, former Vice President Kamala Harris appeared alongside El-Sayed at a roundtable event in Detroit focused on Black maternal health care. 

“Remember, the Senate seat is six years, so let’s think about that in the lives of all the people that the leaders here serve, and the good work that can happen over the course of those years, because of the power and the strength of Abdul and that Senate seat,” Harris told event attendees. 

Former President Obama is also scheduled to campaign with the Democratic nominee on the first day of in-person voting in Michigan on Oct. 24. Obama will also stump for Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson during his visit. 

El-Sayed has narrowly pulled ahead of Rogers in recent polling in this closely contested race, which election handicapper Cook Political Report rates a “toss up.”

During their first debate on Thursday evening, Rogers and El-Sayed jostled over their plans to bring down the cost of living for Michiganders, President Trump’s sinking approval ratings, mass federal immigration crackdowns and the ongoing Iran war.
